nodes.summary: Any `ψ` with `ψ 0 = 0`, `ψ N = 1` that satisfies the first-step equation `ψ i = a_i ψ (i+1) + b_i ψ (i-1) + (1 - a_i - b_i) ψ i` at every `0 < i < N` equals `moranFixation r N` on `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the fixation probability

nodes.summary: Kimura's diffusion fixation probability at scaled selection `σ / 2` is `(1 - e^{-σ x}) / (1 - e^{-σ})` (for `σ ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: Closed form of Kimura's fixation probability

nodes.summary: The down-step probability is nonnegative on the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the Moran down-step probability

nodes.summary: No mutant can be removed when the mutant type is absent.
nodes.title: No down-step from the empty state of the Moran process

nodes.summary: Probability that one step of the Moran process takes the mutant count from `i` to `i - 1`: a wild type is chosen to reproduce (probability `(N - i) / (r i + N - i)`) and a mutant is chosen to die (probability `i / N`). Meaningful for `0 < r` and `i ≤ N`.
nodes.title: Down-step probability of the Moran process

nodes.summary: The fixation probability satisfies `φ_i = a_i φ_{i+1} + b_i φ_{i-1} + (1 - a_i - b_i) φ_i`. This is the first-step equation of the chain for the interior states `0 < i < N`; the identity is algebraic (it follows from `r · b_i = a_i`), so it is stated for every `i ≥ 1`.
nodes.title: First-step equation (Moran 1958)

nodes.summary: A mutant that is already fixed stays fixed: `φ_N = 1` (for `N ≠ 0`).
nodes.title: A fixed mutant stays fixed

nodes.summary: A mutant that is absent is never fixed: `φ_0 = 0`.
nodes.title: An absent mutant is never fixed

nodes.summary: The fixation probability of the Moran process started from `i` mutants out of `N`: `(1 - r⁻¹ ^ i) / (1 - r⁻¹ ^ N)` for `r ≠ 1`, and `i / N` in the neutral case `r = 1`. The model's domain is `0 < r`, `N ≥ 1`, `i ≤ N`; outside it the value is the closed formula evaluated with Lean's total division (e.g. `x / 0 = 0`) and carries no meaning.
nodes.title: Fixation probability of the Moran process

nodes.summary: The Moran process with `N` individuals and mutant relative fitness `r > 0`, as a stochastic matrix on the mutant counts `Fin (N + 1)`.
nodes.title: Moran process as a stochastic matrix

nodes.summary: One-step transition probabilities of the Moran process on the states `Fin (N + 1)`: `a_i` to `i + 1`, `b_i` to `i - 1`, `1 - a_i - b_i` to `i`, and `0` elsewhere.
nodes.title: One-step transition probabilities of the Moran process

nodes.summary: On the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N` the up- and down-step probabilities sum to at most `1`, so the probability `1 - a_i - b_i` of staying is nonnegative.
nodes.title: Moran up- and down-step probabilities sum to at most one

nodes.summary: No mutant can be added when the mutant type is fixed.
nodes.title: No up-step from the fixed state of the Moran process

nodes.summary: The up-step probability is nonnegative on the states `0 ≤ i ≤ N`.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of the Moran up-step probability

nodes.summary: Probability that one step of the Moran process with `N` individuals and mutant relative fitness `r` takes the mutant count from `i` to `i + 1`: a mutant is chosen to reproduce (probability `r i / (r i + N - i)`) and a wild type is chosen to die (probability `(N - i) / N`). Meaningful for `0 < r` and `i ≤ N` (the real subtraction `N - i` is negative for `i > N`).
nodes.title: Up-step probability of the Moran process

nodes.summary: The ratio of the down- and up-step probabilities is `1 / r`: `r · b_i = a_i`.
nodes.title: Ratio of Moran down- and up-step probabilities

nodes.summary: One-step expectation of a function `f` of the mutant count from state `i`: `∑ j, P i j f j = a_i f (i + 1) + b_i f (i - 1) + (1 - a_i - b_i) f i` (the boundary terms vanish at `i = 0` and `i = N`).
nodes.title: One-step expectation under the Moran process

nodes.summary: For `N ≠ 0`, the probability that the Moran chain started at `i` is in state `N` after `t` steps tends to `φ_i` as `t → ∞`. Since `N` absorbs, this `t`-step probability is the probability of fixation by time `t`, so its limit is the probability of eventual fixation.
nodes.title: Fixation probability of the chain

nodes.summary: For `N ≠ 0`, the probability that the Moran chain started at `i` is in state `0` after `t` steps tends to `1 - φ_i`; together with `tendsto_matPow_moranMatrix_last`, absorption at `0` or `N` is certain.
nodes.title: Loss probability of the chain

nodes.summary: With relative fitness `r_N = 1 + σ / N` and initial count `i_N = ⌊x N⌋`, the fixation probability `φ^{(N)}_{i_N}` tends to Kimura's `kimuraFixation (σ / 2) x`, which is `(1 - e^{-σ x}) / (1 - e^{-σ})` for `σ ≠ 0` (`kimuraFixation_half`) and `x` for `σ = 0`. The initial frequency `x` is meaningful in `[0, 1]`; the limit of the closed formula holds for every `x ≥ 0`, so only `0 ≤ x` is assumed (for negative `x`,…
nodes.title: Diffusion limit of the Moran fixation probability
